transcript.text: panasonic nn h98 not heating anymore, any fix?

Often yes, but it depends on confirming the fault first. If it is the inverter board, the fix is usually replacing that board, and that must be done by a qualified microwave engineer because the inside holds dangerous high voltage even when unplugged. From what you have described, the most likely cause is inverter board / HV module [INVERTER machine]. Does it never heat at all, or does it heat then cut out after a repeatable few seconds?
it runs a few seconds then stops and shows H98. every time since yesterday. h98 is what the screen says, model on the back is NN-CD87KSBPQ

H98 on your Panasonic means: Magnetron/HV inverter power fault (same family as H97; inverter not working properly). Next: Identify whether the machine is conventional or inverter (from the model) before considering architecture-specific HV parts. Let me know what you find.
[Safety panel] Don't remove the microwave's casing or try to repair it inside. Parts inside a microwave can hold a dangerous electric charge even after it's unplugged — have it checked by a qualified engineer.
no idea what an inverter is. i gave you the model already, NN-CD87KSBPQ. is it worth fixing? it was about £300

It depends on the repair cost compared with the roughly £300 the microwave cost, and on how old it is and whether it's still under warranty. If it's under warranty, a repair is usually worth pursuing; if not, it's often only worth it when the quote is a modest fraction of a replacement's price. Next: Confirm microwave-safe cookware, a normal power level, and that the door latches firmly. Let me know what you find.
[Safety panel] Don't remove the microwave's casing or try to repair it inside. Parts inside a microwave can hold a dangerous electric charge even after it's unplugged — have it checked by a qualified engineer.
its about 6 years old. dont know about warranty. so is it worth fixing or not?

It depends on what has failed and what the repair would cost compared with a new one. At about 6 years old and roughly £300 new, it can be worth repairing if the fix is a moderate fraction of a replacement price, but probably not if the quote comes close to that. Is it a conventional or an inverter microwave (check the model/rating plate), and does it make an abnormally loud/heavy buzzing when it should be heating?
[Safety panel] Don't remove the microwave's casing or try to repair it inside. Parts inside a microwave can hold a dangerous electric charge even after it's unplugged — have it checked by a qualified engineer.
told you i dont know what an inverter is, the model is NN-CD87KSBPQ. didnt notice any buzzing. just need to know if its worth paying for a repair

It depends on what the fault turns out to be and what the repair quote is compared with a replacement. On a six-year-old model that cost about £300, a repair can be worth it if the fault is minor, but if a major internal part is needed the cost can get close to buying new. Check it isn't on a low power level, defrost, or a grill / combination mode, and that a timed cook was started (not just the clock set). Was it on a low power or another mode (and have you changed it), or was it on full power as normal?
